meta.note: Reader-facing one-sentence summaries for the 85 site stories whose summary was empty (76 twin-pass cards whose detector summary was the judge's reasoning and was removed, plus 9 Ketubot placeholders). Written by reading each story's William Davidson English (Hebrew alongside) in site/data on 2026-11-14; no model or API call. Only what the passage text supports. Keyed by site story id.
meta.removed: 2026-11-14, later: the summaries of the 17 twin-pass cards Simon removed from the site (septimus_site_decisions.json `remove`) were dropped, so no summary is keyed to a story that does not ship; their text is in git history. 68 remain. Later the same day: the 35 written summaries of the cards removed or absorbed in the second twin-pass triage pass were dropped (septimus_site_decisions.json `remove` third batch and `merge`).
meta.second_pass: 2026-11-14, second twin-pass pass (claude-opus-5-5 subagent, no model call): rewritten for ketubot-106a-2-3 (span 3-3 since b43deb2: the Rav Yosef famine story only) and rosh_hashanah-25a-11-11 (shown extended to 25a:11-13); written for the three merged cards (megillah-29a-5-5, sanhedrin-11a-7-7, sanhedrin-104a-8-8), each covering the whole merged story; `overrides` added, replacing a detector summary that is wrong as shown.
meta.overrides: `overrides` {story id: text}: replaces the detector's summary where it is wrong as shown (eruvin-53b-24-24: two runs' summaries concatenated, so it said the same thing twice). Used before any other source.

summaries.avodah_zarah-65b-5-5: When a barrel of libation wine broke and spilled onto the dried figs Boethus ben Zunen was carrying on a ship, the Sages permitted the figs, because the wine spoiled their taste rather than improving it.
summaries.bava_batra-8a-16-16: Rabba imposed a charity contribution on the orphans of the house of bar Maryon, and when Abaye objected that orphans are exempt, Rabba explained that he did it to raise their standing, not to benefit the poor.
summaries.bava_metzia-85b-4-4: During their Torah debates, Rabbi Ḥanina boasted that if the Torah were forgotten he could restore it by his own reasoning, and Rabbi Ḥiyya answered that he was working to ensure it would never be forgotten at all.
summaries.bava_metzia-85b-7-7: Rabbi Zeira dreamed that Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina told him where the Sages sit in the upper realms, and that Rabbi Yoḥanan could not be brought near Rabbi Ḥiyya amid its fiery sparks and burning fires.
summaries.berakhot-19a-9-9: Rabbi Yehuda denied that Akavya ben Mahalalel was ever excommunicated, saying it was Elazar ben Ḥanokh who was ostracized for demeaning handwashing, and that when he died the court placed a large stone on his coffin.
summaries.chagigah-15a-10-10: Aḥer and Rabbi Meir debated a verse comparing Torah to gold and glass; when Aḥer cited Rabbi Akiva that a fallen scholar can be restored, Rabbi Meir urged him to repent, and Aḥer said a heavenly voice had excluded him.
summaries.ketubot-106a-2-3: In a famine during Rav Yosef's years, the Sages asked him to pray for mercy, and he refused, pointing out that the prophet Elisha, who supported 2,200 Sages from his own pocket, did not pray in a time of famine either.
summaries.ketubot-112a-3-4: Seeing grape clusters as large as calves in Gavla, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi lamented that the land fed gentiles, and the next year, when Rabbi Ḥiyya admired clusters the size of goats, the locals told him to go away.
summaries.ketubot-54b-1-2: Rabbi Yoḥanan advised his relatives to have their father set aside land to support his wasteful wife, but after the father died Reish Lakish ordered them to support her fully, and Rabbi Yoḥanan said he could not overrule an equal.
summaries.ketubot-61b-1-1: A Roman ate peeled pomegranates in front of a woman who refused to marry him until she fell ill from craving them, then cured her, once she agreed to marry him, by having her spit out her saliva.
summaries.ketubot-63a-2-2: Rav Yosef son of Rava broke off his six years of study after three to visit his wife on the eve of Yom Kippur, and his father came out armed to confront him; in their quarrel neither ate the meal before the fast.
summaries.ketubot-69b-10-12: Passed over for head of the yeshiva, Ilfa hung from a ship's mast and vowed to fall if he could not trace any baraita of Rabbi Ḥiyya's school to a mishna, and he answered an elder's challenge about a dying father's weekly shekel.
summaries.ketubot-85a-3-4: Ḥama son of Rabba bar Abbahu paid the debt Avimi son of Rabbi Abbahu owed people from Bei Ḥozai, but they kept the debt document, claiming the money covered other debts, and Rabbi Abbahu ruled that they could.
summaries.ketubot-86a-4-4: In a similar case, Rafram pressed Rav Ashi to give a clear ruling, and Rav Ashi collected the full value of the debt written in the promissory note.
summaries.ketubot-91b-2-3: A debtor sold two mansions; when his creditor seized one and sought the other, the buyer offered him a thousand dinars to give up his claim, and Rava, rejecting Rami bar Ḥama's comparison, said refusing would be cruel.
summaries.makkot-16b-6-6: A man ate a fish-like creature found in the furrows of a plowed field, and Rav Yehuda had him flogged for eating a creeping animal.
summaries.moed_katan-21a-6-6: When Rabbi Yosei's son died in Tzippori, Rabbi Yosei went into the study hall and taught there all day, although a mourner is normally barred from Torah study.
summaries.moed_katan-25b-2-2: When Ravina died, a eulogizer began by calling on the date palms to bow their heads for a righteous man like a palm, and to turn nights into days of weeping for one who studied through the night.
summaries.moed_katan-25b-9-9: When Rabbi Yoḥanan died, Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Elazar opened his eulogy by saying the day was as hard for Israel as the day the sun set at noon, the verse Rabbi Yoḥanan had applied to King Josiah's death.
summaries.pesachim-49a-15-15: Rav Idi bar Avin married a priest's daughter and had two ordained sons, Rav Sheshet and Rabbi Yehoshua, and Rav Pappa said he became wealthy only because he too married a priest's daughter.
summaries.pesachim-51a-2-2: When Yehuda and Hillel, sons of Rabban Gamliel, bathed together in Kabul, where brothers did not, the whole city denounced them, and Hillel slipped out to the outer chamber rather than tell them it was permitted.
summaries.rosh_hashanah-18a-7-7: Rabba and Abaye both descended from the house of Eli, whose members were cursed to die young; Rabba, who devoted himself to Torah, lived forty years, while Abaye, who added acts of kindness, lived sixty.
summaries.rosh_hashanah-25a-11-11: Rabbi Akiva found Rabbi Yehoshua distressed that Rabban Gamliel was forcing him to desecrate the day he reckoned as Yom Kippur, and consoled him with a teaching Yehoshua had once taught him: the day the court fixes is sanctified even if it errs, and Yehoshua said, "Akiva, you have consoled me."
summaries.sanhedrin-52b-3-3: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok recalled a priest's daughter who committed adultery being executed by actual burning, and the Sages told him the court then was not proficient; Rav Yosef says it was a Sadducee court.
summaries.shabbat-115b-1-1: When Rabbi Yishmael climbed a ladder in Sidon to confront a man writing blessings, the scribe sank the bundle in a basin of water, and Rabbi Yishmael told him that destroying them was worse than writing them.
summaries.shabbat-23b-3-3: Seeing Rabbi Avin the carpenter kindle many Shabbat lights, Rav Huna foretold that two great men would come from his house, and his sons Rav Idi and Rav Ḥiyya did; Rav Ḥisda likewise foresaw Rav Sheizvi from his father's lamps.
summaries.taanit-21b-8-8: When told that locusts had come but were eating very little, Rav Yehuda decreed a fast anyway, asking whether the locusts had brought their own provisions.
summaries.yevamot-105a-13-13: Rabba and Abaye, descendants of the house of Eli, outlived that family's curse of early death: Rabba, who devoted himself to Torah study, lived forty years, and Abaye, who added acts of kindness, lived sixty.
summaries.yevamot-121b-14-14: Hearing a gentile call out that Ḥivvai had died, Rav Yosef allowed Ḥivvai's wife to remarry, and when another gentile lamented a dead horseman of Pumbedita, Rav Yosef, or some say Rava, let his wife remarry too.
summaries.yevamot-34b-6-6: Rava told his wife, Rav Ḥisda's daughter, that the Sages were gossiping because she bore him children after more than ten years of widowhood, and she answered that her mind had always been on him.
summaries.yevamot-63a-6-6: Seeing a field plowed across its width, Rabbi Elazar told it that even if it were plowed lengthwise as well, business would still pay better than farming it.
summaries.yoma-38b-2-2: Ben Kamtzar could write a four-letter word at once with four quills between his fingers but refused to teach the skill, and unlike others who guarded their techniques, he had no reason but his own honor.
summaries.yoma-83b-9-9: Rabbi Yoḥanan recalled that when he was seized with bulmos, a ravenous faintness, he ran to the east side of a fig tree, found ripe figs there and ate them, fulfilling the verse that wisdom preserves life.
summaries.megillah-29a-5-5: When the Divine Presence came to the synagogue in Neharde'a, Shmuel's father and Levi heard a loud sound and left, but the blind Rav Sheshet stayed, and when the ministering angels tried to frighten him out, he pleaded with God, who told them to leave him.
summaries.sanhedrin-11a-7-7: A Divine Voice in Yavne marked Shmuel HaKatan as worthy of prophecy; at his death the Sages mourned him as a pious and humble man and he foretold the coming persecutions, and they wished to mourn Yehuda ben Bava the same way but could not, because the government had executed him.
summaries.sanhedrin-104a-8-8: Rabbi Perida's grandfather found a skull inscribed "This and yet another" that would not stay buried, recognised it as King Jehoiakim's and kept it wrapped in silk in a box, until his wife, thinking it was his first wife's, burned it.
summaries.avodah_zarah-17b-3-13: The Romans arrested Rabbi Elazar ben Perata on five charges and Rabbi Hanina ben Teradyon on one.
summaries.avodah_zarah-39a-9-9: Rav Ashi came to a certain place where he was served a fish that looked like a shefarnuna.
summaries.bava_kamma-112a-13-14: Rabbi Yirmeya's brother-in-law, a minor, shut the doors of his late father's house against Rabbi Yirmeya, who claimed part of it.
summaries.bava_metzia-42a-11-11: A man left money in another's care.
summaries.kiddushin-70a-11-16: In a Pumbedita butcher shop, a man from Neharde'a was told to wait until Rav Yehuda bar Yeḥezkel's servant was served, and mocked Rav Yehuda with an insulting name.
summaries.menachot-103b-18-20: Rabbi Beivai reported, in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, that a mule belonging to the household of Rabbi died and the Sages estimated its blood at a quarter-log.
summaries.tamid-31b-14-14: Alexander of Macedon put ten questions to the Elders of the Negev: about distances, the order of creation (they declined to say whether light or darkness came first), who is wise, mighty and rich, how to live and how to die.
summaries.bava_batra-58a-8-10: A dying man left one son a barrel of earth, another a barrel of bones, and a third a barrel of wool wads; Rabbi Bena'a worked out that he meant land, livestock and quilts.
summaries.moed_katan-9a-19-22: Two disciples, Rabbi Yonatan ben Asmai and Rabbi Yehuda, son of converts, took leave of their teacher Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai in the evening and came back to take leave again in the morning, explaining that he had taught them a disciple who stays the night in the same city must do so twice.

overrides.eruvin-53b-24-24: Berurya found a student whispering his studies and kicked him, explaining from a verse that Torah is retained only when it is studied with one's whole body.
